guide.title: Read and test a modern prism illustration
guide.goal: Separate declared ray geometry from a measured optical reconstruction.
prerequisites: Use source millimetres and the declared ray-angle conventions.
Use diffuse, low-intensity white-LED illumination and a replica arrangement; do not substitute direct sun viewing or a laser.

steps.title: Start with the pinned model
instructions: Open the source record and attached contract; write down the observed quantity, units and rival explanation.
Run the existing numerical controls before selecting physical parts; record the exact source commit and original parameter conventions.
checks: A completed software test is not a completed apparatus test.
stopIf: The contract or source identity is missing, or its peak/RMS and unit convention is unresolved.

steps.title: Specify a nonhazardous replica
instructions: Use the pinned ray drawing as a desk prediction, then document actual prism geometry, material and illumination.
Record the aperture, screen and axis references before comparing ray positions.
checks: Label changed geometry or material as a new replica scenario.
stopIf: Verified material/geometry information or suitable illumination is unavailable.

steps.title: Compare predicted and observed positions
instructions: Record repeat images with fixed camera and screen references while varying incidence.
Treat a second-prism control as a separately documented study.
checks: Report wavelength and angle calibration with uncertainty.
stopIf: Dispersion, alignment or source extent cannot be bounded.

requirements.label: Drawing sheet size
requirements.rule: US §1.84(f): A4 210×297mm or US Letter216×279mm; EPO A49Art2(2)/PCT11.5 use A4 (PCT receiving-office exception does not alter A4 record-copy rule).

requirements.label: Drawing margins and sight
requirements.rule: US1.84(g), A49Art1(1), PCT11.6(c): minimum top25,left25,right15,bottom10mm; A4 sight no greater than170×262mm; no frame around usable area.

requirements.label: Reference-number and letter height
requirements.rule: US1.84(p)(3), A49Art1(2)(g), PCT11.13(h): drawing numbers/letters at least3.2mm high. Do not substitute EPO2.1mm description text minimum.

requirements.label: Two-thirds reproduction readability
requirements.rule: US1.84(k), A49Art1(2)(c), PCT11.13(c): details remain distinguishable after linear reduction to two-thirds; requires actual legibility review, not only a numeric SVG test.

requirements.label: Monochrome common profile
requirements.rule: US1.84(a),(l) and PCT11.13(a) support black-line default. A49Art1(2)(a) allows electronically filed colour/greyscale with contrast/300dpi suitability; monochrome here is a conservative profile choice.

requirements.label: Keep lengthy explanation off drawing sheet
requirements.rule: A49Art1(2)(j), PCT11.11 permit only indispensable short words; keep full definitions, products and teaching prose in separate description/reference documents.

requirements.label: Stable reference signs and cross-reference legend
requirements.rule: US1.84(p)(4)–(5), A49Art1(2)(i), PCT11.13(l)–(n): same feature uses same sign; drawing/description references correspond; separate feature list is useful.

requirements.label: Unambiguous leader lines
requirements.rule: US1.84(q): short lines from near character to feature, noncrossing; surface/section exception uses underline. Reference signs must not obscure drawing lines/hatching.

requirements.label: Sufficient distinct views
requirements.rule: US1.84(h)–(j), A49Art1(2)(h), PCT11.13(i)–(k): necessary views separated, not overlapping; partial views assemble without obscuring detail.

requirements.label: Figure and sheet numbers are separate
requirements.rule: US1.84(u): sequential FIG.1 etc, larger than reference signs; a single-view US application must have neither view number nor FIG. EPO/PCT sequential Arabic figure numbering is independent of sheets.

requirements.label: Sheet numbering placement
requirements.rule: US1.84(t): if present, sheet/total format and larger than reference characters within sight; EPOA49Art2(5) top-centred not in margin; PCT11.7 top/bottom-centred not margin.

requirements.label: US scan targets are recommended, not mandatory
requirements.rule: US1.84(g) says sheets should have scan target crosshairs on two catercorner margin corners. This is not a four-marker must requirement and not an EPO/PCT common mandate.

requirements.label: Cross-section hatching
requirements.rule: US1.84(h)(3), A49Art1(2)(b), PCT11.13(b): hatching should remain distinguishable and not impede reference signs/leaders. No section/material is inferred where source geometry is absent.

requirements.label: Proportions and scale indications
requirements.rule: US1.84(k) prohibits actual-size/scale1/2 indications. EPO/PCT exceptional scale indications use a graphic scale; preserve proportions unless a clarity exception is explicit.

requirements.label: Separate description structure
requirements.rule: EPC Rule42(1)(a)–(f): field, useful known background, problem/solution and advantageous effects, brief figures, at least one detailed way of carrying out, industrial applicability when not obvious. US1.71(a)–(c) asks full/clear making-and-using description.

requirements.label: Define symbols and reference features without changing conventions
requirements.rule: Explain source-dependent units, peak/RMS conventions and feature functions in the description/reference table; distinguish this educational completeness policy from a claim that every symbol is legally prescribed.

requirements.label: Claim language and support
requirements.rule: EPC Art84 and Rule43: clear concise supported technical features, proper dependency/numbering; claims cannot merely say as shown in a figure; reference signs in claims are parenthesised where useful.

requirements.label: Enablement is separate from drawing mechanics
requirements.rule: US1.71/MPEP2164 and EPCArt83/F-III1 require sufficient making/using information for a skilled person without undue experimentation/burden. Unknown essential turns/ratings/calibration or unproven effects remain gaps, not invented values.

requirements.label: Later drawings cannot silently add original disclosure
requirements.rule: MPEP608.02 quotes35USC113/37CFR1.81(d): later drawings cannot cure missing enabling disclosure or supplement original claim scope. EPCArt123(2) forbids extension beyond content as filed; label new educational geometry as new authored material.

requirements.label: Proposed examples and operated setups remain separate
requirements.rule: For this product, record whether an example is a source assertion, hypothetical procedure, deterministic model or measured apparatus. No mechanical-sheet check establishes physical validation or claim sufficiency.

requirements.label: Scratch setup document is an educational extension
requirements.rule: A reader setup guide should list known components, tools, units, prerequisites, interfaces, measurement/calibration plan, controls and missing specifications; standards address the skilled person, not a guarantee of novice buildability.

improvements.title: Evaluate synthetic late reverberation separately from measured room response
improvements.proposal: Retain the raw measured response and deterministic early-reflection baseline. In a separate optional research branch, compare a predicted late tail with held-out measured rooms and clearly label all inferred samples.
improvements.rationale: The 2025 DECOR full-text discussion identifies unseen-room generalization losses. A modelled tail is useful for auralization while retaining the measurement and inference boundary.
requiredValidation: Review code/data licenses before any model import; no model is downloaded or added here.
Keep held-out rooms separate from training or tuning.
Record sampling rate, excitation, microphone calibration, source and receiver positions and processing.

improvements.title: Log frequency, supply and tuning state as separate control variables
improvements.proposal: Define a separate controlled-excitation test branch whose experimental log records drive frequency, supply voltage, selected capacitor configuration and source power at each step.
improvements.rationale: A recent 2026 application distinguishes these control variables. Keeping them separately recorded prevents an apparent improvement caused by an unnoticed input-power change.
requiredValidation: Preserve the frozen source baseline and proposed branch as different revisions.
Document all switched capacitance ratings, transient limits and controller/converter auxiliary power before assembly.
Run fixed-load and fixed-source controls with calibrated simultaneous voltage/current acquisition.
Compare total energy and uncertainty, not receiver voltage alone.

improvements.title: Separate input, branch and load energy measurement boundaries
improvements.proposal: Create a commissioning worksheet with independently identified input, transfer-branch and receiving-load energy channels, signed polarity and start/end storage states.
improvements.rationale: The 2026 application explicitly distinguishes input and distributed energy accounting. The transferable research question is boundary completeness; its road-metering implementation is not adopted.
requiredValidation: Calibrate each voltage/current channel including phase and clock alignment.
Include internal loss, external supports/auxiliary sources and endpoint stored energy.
Compare an independent energy quadrature with the original solver accounting.
Do not equate current allocation with measured load energy without the corresponding voltage and phase.

improvements.title: Test load-state transition timing and feedback delay
improvements.proposal: Preregister a test for whether load changes, acquisition timing or delayed feedback can create apparent power-gain peaks; keep fixed-state baselines and state-transition receipts.
improvements.rationale: The 2026 application identifies load states, coupling references and synchronization. They motivate controls for transient artifacts before any adaptive control is added.
requiredValidation: Log the exact source, load and feedback state against a shared clock.
Compare delayed and exchanged-channel controls.
Measure rather than infer coupling from gap or a product name.
Record every drive/controller supply and validate stability before a hardware fork.
